title: Cross-corpus eval: schedule_change_announcement v2_elided on Hadoop common-dev@ 2014
description:
Cross-corpus generalization test (U1) for schedule_change_announcement on Hadoop common-dev@ 2014. Pre-reg block in docs/experiment-log.md (2026-05-03 si-2wh entry).

INPUTS (frozen):
- Corpus: data/processed/apache/common-dev@hadoop.apache.org/2014-*.jsonl (3503 messages)
- Operating point: schedule_change_announcement v2_elided (frozen prompt-hash ba10bafd2d271613)
- Eval harness: src/evaluate/pool_and_extrapolate.py v0.2.0

EXECUTE:
1. Filter step (NEW): write src/harvest/filter_bots.py — drop messages where from_email == 'jira@apache.org' OR from_email ends with '@builds.apache.org'. Output: data/processed/apache/common-dev@hadoop.apache.org-filtered/2014-*.jsonl. Pre-flight verified: 3503 → 1355 human-authored messages.
2. Run cheap-tier on filtered corpus: python3 -m src.classify.schedule_change_announcement --corpus-dir data/processed/apache/common-dev@hadoop.apache.org-filtered --out results/detector-runs/schedule_change_announcement/si-2wh/hadoop-common-dev-2014-predictions-v2-elided.jsonl --quote-depth 2 --prompt-variant v2_elided --concurrency 32 --no-logprobs
3. Spawn clean Opus subagent for pool-and-extrapolate labeling. Inputs: filtered corpus + cheap-tier predictions + v2 rubric ONLY (anti-contamination — no Cassandra labels, no prior rationales, no this pre-reg). Hand-label all model-positives + 50 random model-negatives. Apply v2 rubric verbatim. Output: labels/schedule_change_announcement/hadoop-common-dev-2014-labels-v2.jsonl with sample_role ∈ {pool, random_sample}.
4. Score: src/evaluate/pool_and_extrapolate.py against the new labels. Pool-direct precision, extrapolated recall, F1.

DECISION RULE: F1 within ±0.10 of Cassandra cheap-tier 0.5556 (i.e., 0.46-0.66) ⇒ generalizing; promote to Validated-on-2-corpora; advance to si-03o (frontier+escalation transfer). F1 > 0.66 ⇒ better than expected; verify by hand-sampling. F1 < 0.46 ⇒ over-fit to Cassandra; document failure modes; do NOT retune in this bead.

ANTI-CONTAMINATION: subagent labels Hadoop messages with v2 rubric only — must not see Cassandra labels, prior rationales, or the pre-reg block.

Then: write Results block to experiment-log.md, commit, close si-2wh with --reason referencing commit hash. File any follow-up ideas (e.g., rubric-adaptation if F1 low; subject-marker convention findings).

title: MessageContext substrate — full design (umbrella idea)
description: Umbrella idea capturing the full substrate vision per the user's strategic guidance (memory: messages_are_not_single_thesis_streams.md). Treats freeform messages as structured artifacts with derived fields: new_content, quoted_segments[], thread_position (depth/parent/root/siblings), temporal_position (timestamp, project-state-at-time pointers), author_context (recent activity, role, prior topics), cross_thread_context (parallel-thread activity), tags (typed properties + embedding-derived). Each piece is a separate bd issue with its own test gate. This umbrella tracks the overall lattice and the architectural-doc update that should follow once 2-3 substrate pieces have proved themselves on real detector work. Connects to U4 (signal density), U5 (affective signal), U8 (dependency graph reconstruction).

title: Typed-tag extraction over messages — JIRA refs, version refs, [VOTE] markers, register
description: Idea-stage. Motivated by Op-6 ('Alright, let's wait on 7743') — a 6-word reply where the schedule-change semantics depend on knowing 7743 is an open blocker JIRA. The cheap-tier model can't bridge that without help, but a structured tag layer (JIRA-ref extraction + JIRA-state lookup) would let a downstream detector reason: 'message references an OPEN JIRA in vote-context → schedule change.' Other tags worth extracting: version mentions ('2.1.0', '3.0'), named release markers ('[VOTE]', '[VOTE CLOSED]', '[VOTE PASSED]', '[VOTE RESURRECTED]'), code-block presence, register classifier (formal vote-process / technical discussion / coordination). Each tag is a single-thesis extraction pass per the architectural commitment. Earn one tag at a time by demonstrating a detector that needs it.
notes: si-rrz result (2026-05-02): typed-tag substrate now has concrete success metric. v2_elided lost 3 specific TPs that all require version-state-at-time disambiguation: Op-9 (Sylvain 'I'd prefer doing a quick re-roll of 1.2.18'), Shuler ('Should this be fixed for a 1.2.18 re-roll?'), Ellis ('I'd even lean towards taking 1.2.17 down until that's fixed'). Each requires inferring whether a referenced version number is NEW (proposed) vs NEXT (routine patch sequence). When this issue is built, success = recovers these 3 TPs without introducing new FPs against the existing 153-item OpusLabel-v2 pool. F1 lift target: 0.769 → ~0.86 if all 3 are recovered cleanly.
close_reason: Results committed in 774fdb0. Counterintuitive REGRESSION: v2_elided_tagged F1=0.667 vs v2_elided's 0.769. Substrate built correct version-state data but cheap-tier interpreted it in opposite direction (anti-anchoring on procedural frame). 0/3 dropped TPs recovered. Critical U3 finding: substrate demand must be tested, not inferred. Awaiting si-2z6 to disambiguate capability vs prompt-structure ceiling.

title: Cross-thread same-author context index
description: Idea-stage. User flagged this explicitly as fundamental: 'parallel threads at the same time with a shared author — that's important context and we need to be able to find it when we want to.' Build an index that, for any (author, message_timestamp), returns the author's parallel-thread activity within a configurable time window (e.g., ±7 days, excluding the current thread). Required for: author-baseline detectors (affective signal, U5), discovering when an author's tone shifts across topics, distinguishing 'is this author always like this' from 'is this message anomalous for them.' Storage substrate is open: SQLite/Postgres index, or a precomputed JSONL augment. Earn it by demonstrating one detector that needs it; until then, idea-stage.

Score each against OpusLabels. Compare per-message flips. Specifically check: does Op-13 (Jonathan, anchored on Benedict's quoted text) flip from cheap-tier-positive to cheap-tier-negative under (A) and (B)? Do Op-5 / Op-6 (the two cheap-tier-FN OpusPositives) move? Decision rule and falsifiers in the pre-reg.

title: Add new_content / quoted_segments / attribution_lines extraction to message parsing
description: Smallest first piece of the MessageContext substrate. Today the classifier sees raw body_text filtered by quote depth, and the cheap-tier model can't distinguish quoted material from new content (documented across si-bwo, si-fnw, si-pfo). Add a function (likely in src/classify/quote_extractor.py or a new src/structure/message_context.py) that splits a body into: (1) new_content — lines this author wrote in this message, after stripping quoted lines, attribution scaffolding ('On Mon, X wrote:'), and signature blocks; (2) quoted_segments[] — each quoted block with its quote depth; (3) attribution_lines[] — the structural 'X wrote:' lines, neither new nor quoted but worth preserving for analysis. No corpus reprocessing required for the first cut — derive at classify time. If the prompt-variant experiment (filed separately) shows value, formalize this into the harvest pipeline as a real corpus field.

title: Depth sweep: quote-aware excision for schedule_change_announcement
description: From si-bwo and the user's 'local temporal context' observation: the model anchors on whatever quoted block is in front of it. Test whether systematically controlling quote-depth exposure recovers signal. Run the same classifier prompt at depths {0, 1, 2, infinity} on the 731-message corpus, compare against existing labels (which are message-scoped, so they transfer). Sweet spot expected at depth 0 or 1 for this detector. Establishes a reusable pattern (per memory: local_temporal_context.md) for future detectors. Per pre-reg discipline, write a new pre-reg with predictions for each depth before running. Deferred si-d6m (rubric sharpening) until this completes — sweep results may inform the rubric.
close_reason: Results landed in commit 1000530. Best F1=0.405 at depth=2 (vs my predicted depth=0). 'Less context is better' theory falsified; the model needs parent+grandparent context to disambiguate references in brief replies. Detector still below promotion threshold. Adopt depth=2 as default for si-d6m. Brier divergence 0.07-0.20 across depths confirms calibration maps must be per-(detector, depth).

title: Fix eval harness stratification bug
description: From si-bwo: when items move between pool and random_sample across runs (e.g., due to a parameter change like the body cap), the harness mixes the original random_sample (uniformly drawn) with the moved items (selected on flipping condition) as if they were one sample. The 6 flipped items in si-bwo's merged eval came in as if they were random_sample additions. Fix: separate the strata in the harness, compute recall as (TP / (TP + FN_extrapolated_from_random + FN_explicit_in_other_strata)). Or accept additional pool labels separately from sample additions in the labels schema.
close_reason: Stratified FN estimation by sample_role committed in 1a23fa4. Verified on v2_elided (recall 0.254 → 0.625), v2_strict (1.000 unchanged), v1 baseline (0.496 → 0.638). Two new tests in src/evaluate/test_pool_and_extrapolate.py. Backward compatible via legacy fallback for label files without sample_role.

title: Re-run classifier with relaxed body cap; check for flipped predictions
description: From si-qhz: 40/731 messages had body_text > 8000 chars and were truncated by the classifier's input cap. Token usage analysis showed max prompt was 3.4K tokens (11% of the 32K window), so the cap was conservative. Bump it to 100,000 chars (still safely under context budget given ~4 chars/token), re-run only the 40 affected messages, compare against original predictions. Any prediction that flips because the model now sees the full body affects the eval — re-run pool-and-extrapolate if so. Treat the original run as authoritative for the pre-reg; this is a methodological audit, not a re-do.
close_reason: Audit landed in commit 4a13f72. Cap bumped from 8000 to 60000 chars. Headline numbers unchanged (F1 0.39 -> 0.36); the real finding is that the cap-bump introduced a NEW false positive by exposing previously-truncated quoted content. The model's failure mode is fundamentally about not distinguishing quoted from new content, not about input length. Dovetails with si-d6m (rubric sharpening should include a quote-stripping step).

title: Sharpen schedule_change_announcement rubric and re-pre-register
description: From si-qhz Results: F1=0.389 was driven by rubric ambiguity, not model capability. The frozen rubric in commit 7d64413 leaves underspecified: (a) how to label '+1'/'-1' replies that quote a parent announcement, (b) whether substantive replies in a schedule-discussion thread that don't propose changes themselves count, (c) whether standard release votes count as 'schedule changes' (the model says yes, my strict reading says no). Sharpen each, write a new pre-reg, re-label the existing 148 items. Existing predictions can be re-evaluated against the new labels at zero inference cost.
notes:
si-s9y completed: best F1 envelope is depth=2 (parent+grandparent), not depth=0. Re-pre-register rubric work AT DEPTH=2 — feed the model the depth=2 view when applying the new rubric. The original 'strict reading' issue is still unresolved; depth alone gets us from F1 0.31 to 0.40, and rubric work is the remaining lever.
si-pfo result (2026-05-02): noise floor at depth=2 is F1 ±0.015, so this rubric work can use single-run scorecards; multi-run aggregation not needed for effects ≥0.04. Bonus: si-pfo incidentally produced the **rubric stress-test set** at zero cost. The 15 messages that flip across the 6 reruns are exactly the rubric-ambiguity boundary — dominated by '[VOTE]', '[VOTE CLOSED]', and 'Proposed changes to C* Release Schedule' subjects (Michael Kjellman, Sylvain Lebresne, Brandon Williams, etc.). Any v2 rubric that doesn't cleanly classify all 15 hasn't sharpened the right thing. List in results/evals/schedule_change_announcement-pfo-noise-floor/summary.json under 'unstable_messages'. Also: lone-TP at depth=2 (Jonathan Ellis 'I plan to address this... after 3.0' message) is structurally stable but anchors on quoted Benedict text rather than Jonathan's actual reply — see si-pfo-reruns/lone-tp-diagnostic.md. A rubric edit that instructs the model to ignore quoted lines will lose this TP. Trade-off worth quantifying before adopting that rubric direction.
si-clz result (2026-05-02): rubric work is now MORE clearly the gating issue, not less. The prompt-variant test showed substrate change is too coarse — it removes both anchoring-failures and productive-uses-of-context. Net F1 regressed (0.405 → 0.21) under both variants A and B. The 11 'regression' messages cluster on the rubric-ambiguous boundary: is 're-roll' a schedule change or vote-process routine? Substrate didn't resolve this; only rubric work can. Combined rubric stress-test set for si-d6m now: - The 15 unstable messages from si-pfo (subjects [VOTE], [VOTE CLOSED], 'Release Schedule') - The 11 'regression' messages from si-clz (where new_content has a schedule keyword but the cheap-tier without context interpreted it as routine) — listed in results/evals/schedule_change_announcement-clz-variants/summary.json under 'c_to_ab_flip_diagnostics' with interpretation='regression' - The 17 'anchoring fix' messages from si-clz are the FP-side stress-test: a sharpened rubric using depth=2 should NOT call these positive (they're listed under interpretation='anchoring fix' in the same JSON) Total ~26 boundary messages plus 17 should-be-negatives. Any v2 rubric must cleanly resolve all 26 in some direction and correctly negative the 17. Also: si-clz committed parse repair + new_content truncation in 1f9cdf7 — minor improvements to schedule_change_announcement.py.
close_reason: Closed via si-rrz (9a24e9e). schedule_change_announcement promoted to Prototype. v2 rubric (3313c2a) + v2_elided body shape (277d52f) is the operating point. F1 = 0.769, precision = 1.000, recall (pool) = 0.625 against OpusLabel-v2.

title: Cost-tier escalation foray: cheap-tier triages, frontier resolves borderline cases
description:
Cost-tier escalation simulation on existing data (no new LLM inference). Pre-reg block in docs/experiment-log.md (2026-05-03 entry, sub-experiment 2).

INPUTS (frozen):
- Cheap predictions: results/detector-runs/schedule_change_announcement/si-d6m/cassandra-2014-predictions-v2-elided.jsonl
- Frontier predictions: results/detector-runs/schedule_change_announcement/si-2z6/cassandra-2014-predictions-frontier-v2-elided.jsonl
- Labels (post-si-e5q expanded): labels/schedule_change_announcement/cassandra-2014-labels-v2.jsonl

CRITICAL FINDING (informs pre-reg, must be reported as observation):
- Cheap-tier p_positive distribution is bimodal: 726 items at p_pos<0.01, 5 at p_pos>0.90, ZERO in [0.01, 0.90]. Logprob-based borderline criterion is structurally unavailable. Borderline criterion uses content-structural rules instead.

POOLS TO EVALUATE (computed against cheap-tier model-NEGATIVES; full definitions in pre-reg):
- P0 (control): no escalation
- P1 (~46): NEG ∩ X.Y.Z body ∩ release-keyword ∩ NOT [VOTE]-root subj
- P2 (~241): NEG ∩ vote/proposal-marker subject ∩ (root OR body>800)
- P3 (~282): NEG ∩ vote/proposal-marker subject (any reply)
- P_full (726): all NEG escalated

OUTPUTS:
- src/evaluate/analyze_bm1_escalation.py (new analysis script; no LLM inference)
- results/evals/schedule_change_announcement-bm1-escalation/scorecard.json with per-pool {pool_size, n_frontier_calls, recovered_TPs, new_FPs, precision, recall, F1}.

EXECUTE: write the analysis script following the simulation logic spelled out in pre-reg ('cheap on confident, frontier on borderline'). Run it. Score against post-si-e5q labels.

DECISION RULE: smallest pool P_min where combined-F1 >= 0.90 AND within 0.05 of P_full is the production operating point. If no pool clears 0.85, document.

Then: write Results block, commit, close si-bm1 with --reason referencing commit hash. File any follow-up ideas (e.g., test the operating-point pool on Hadoop corpus).
close_reason: Cost-tier escalation simulation validated: P2 pool (33% of corpus) reaches F1=0.960 within 0.003 of full-frontier 0.963. Adopt as production operating point. Results in docs/experiment-log.md.

title: Pre-register: Quantify vLLM non-determinism at the prediction level
description: Pre-register block for si-pfo. The closing note carries the commit hash as the receipt that we didn't move the goalposts after seeing the noise.
close_reason: Pre-reg block committed in e18ca39. si-pfo (run) is now unblocked.

title: Quantify vLLM non-determinism at the prediction level
description: From si-s9y: depth=999 sweep differed from si-bwo merged baseline by 17 predictions (out of 731), F1 difference 0.04, despite temperature=0. The differences flip in both directions (POS↔neg) suggesting genuine non-determinism rather than a one-sided bias. Methodologically important: future detector experiments need to know the per-run noise floor to interpret scorecard differences correctly. Quick experiment: run the same input through the classifier 5 times, measure cross-run prediction agreement and F1 spread. Goal is a calibrated noise floor (e.g., '±0.04 F1 is within run-to-run noise; larger differences are signal').
close_reason: Results committed in 92e71da. F1 noise floor at depth=2 is ±0.015 (5x smaller than the si-fnw depth=2-vs-plateau gap), confirming the depth=2 winner is real signal not stochastic. si-d6m can proceed with single-run scorecards. 15 unstable messages identified as the rubric stress-test set for si-d6m.

title: Calibrate logprobs via Platt or isotonic regression
description: From si-qhz: raw Qwen3 logprobs are extremely overconfident (top-bin predicted 0.99, actual fraction positive 0.30). Brier 0.215 says raw probabilities aren't trustworthy. Apply Platt scaling or isotonic regression on the labeled set, re-measure Brier and reliability. Quick test of whether post-hoc calibration is sufficient for downstream synthesis to use these probabilities.

title: Frontier-tier ceiling check for schedule_change_announcement
description: Per pre-reg's <0.50 falsifier: run Sonnet 4.6 on the same 148 hand-labeled items. Disambiguates 'task is hard' from 'cheap-tier model is bad at this.' Deferred from si-qhz because rubric sharpening is the more pressing finding, but valuable for U3 (cost-tier hierarchy).
notes: si-s9y completed: ceiling check should run frontier model at depth=2 (best envelope this model achieves), not depth=999. Cleanly disambiguates 'task is hard' from 'cheap-tier model is bad at this envelope'.
close_reason: Results committed in a64484c. Frontier ceiling F1=0.941; all 3 cheap-tier-v2_elided dropped TPs recovered from same elided body (Op-9, Shuler 1.2.18, Ellis 1.2.17 takedown). 5 unlabeled discoveries filed as si-e5q. Cost-tier escalation idea (si-bm1) and few-shot scaffolding idea (si-q0i) filed. Confirms the cheap-tier capability ceiling (not substrate ceiling) is the gap.

title: Investigate code-block-message bias in classifier inputs
description: From si-qhz: messages that triggered markdown-fence wrapping (and thus initial parser failures) were 10x enriched for model-positives (17.3% vs 1.6% in the first batch). Suggests messages with code blocks BOTH trigger markdown wrapping AND discuss release-related code work. Investigate whether this correlation generalizes — is 'has code block' itself a feature for downstream detectors?

title: Harvest a second multi-org corpus
description:
Harvest Hadoop dev@ 2014 as the second corpus. Pre-reg block in docs/experiment-log.md (2026-05-03 entry, sub-experiment 1). Concrete spec:

INPUTS: lists.apache.org mbox.lua API (existing src/harvest/apache_mbox.py), list=dev, domain=hadoop.apache.org, range 2014-01..2014-12.

OUTPUTS:
- data/raw/apache/dev@hadoop.apache.org/2014-MM.mbox (12 files)
- data/processed/apache/dev@hadoop.apache.org/2014-MM.jsonl (12 files)
- A diversity report committed inline in the Results block: top-10 senders, their email-domains, and the count of distinct domains.

EXECUTE: python -m src.harvest.apache_mbox --list dev --domain hadoop.apache.org --start 2014-01 --end 2014-12

DECISION RULE (post-harvest):
- Top-10 sender domains span >=3 distinct orgs AND total messages >=1000: corpus accepted; close si-t3l with success and file 'idea' follow-up to run schedule_change_announcement v2_elided cross-corpus.
- <3 orgs OR <1000 messages: do NOT promote; close with reason='single-org-ish' and file an idea-status bd issue to evaluate alternative corpus.

ANTI-CONTAMINATION: do NOT inspect Hadoop messages for schedule-change content during this foray.

Then: write Results block to experiment-log.md, commit code+data, close si-t3l with --reason referencing the commit hash.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Decision documented in docs/datasets.md or experiment-log.md noting which corpus and why. (2) Harvester runs successfully against it, producing JSONL under data/processed/. (3) Sender-affiliation diversity verified (top-10 senders span 3+ distinct organizations).
close_reason: Hadoop common-dev@ 2014 harvested (3503 messages); top-10 sender domains span 4 distinct, multi-org coordination texture confirmed. Results in docs/experiment-log.md (2026-05-03 entry).

title: Extend cost-tier-escalation borderline criterion to catch lateral version-discussion messages (e.g., '2.1 rc3?')
description: si-bm1 P2 missed 1 of 8 known frontier-positives: 'CALdd-zjZ2MZu0...' subject '2.1 rc3?' — a 251-char Ellis question without [VOTE]/Proposal: subject marker. The shape is 'subject mentions a version pattern + question mark'. Possibly extend P2 to include subjects matching '\b\d+\.\d+\s+rc\d+\??\b'. Low priority — single-message recall improvement.

title: Harvest Hadoop hdfs-dev/mapreduce-dev/yarn-dev sublists for cross-sublist coverage
description: Hadoop's split-list architecture means common-dev (now harvested) is one of four substantive sublists. For more-comprehensive multi-org Hadoop signal, also harvest hdfs-dev, mapreduce-dev, yarn-dev for 2014. Volumes from probe: common-dev 2.7MB/Jan, hdfs-dev 2.3MB, mapreduce-dev 0.6MB, yarn-dev 2.6MB.

title: Investigate Op-13 regression under v2_elided_fewshot (shape-budget hypothesis)
description: si-q0i found that v2_elided_fewshot lost Op-13 (Jonathan 'schema change in 2.1, 3.0 file-based hint storage') as a TP that v2_elided baseline catches. Hypothesis: the cheap-tier has a 'shape budget' — adding worked examples crowds out previously-recognized patterns. Test: compare evidence_quotes and rationales for Op-13 between v2_elided and v2_elided_fewshot.
